prompts.text:
Define a tactile, skeuomorphic Button component with five variants, from
strongest to weakest: primary, secondary, tertiary, ghost, text.
If the project already has a component library or design system, do not
add a new component: restyle its existing Button through its own variant
and token system, and keep its API, props and accessibility as they are.
Otherwise create one reusable Button with `variant` and `size` props.

Style: calm and precise, like the Lumno browser extension and the Cloudflare
dashboard. Neutral grays only, no brand hues. Lit from straight above.
No glossy Web 2.0 shine, no glow, no large blur.

Variants:
1. primary   - near-black slate face (#404859 -> #273042), white label
2. secondary - raised white key (#FFFFFF -> #F4F5F7), dark gray label
3. tertiary  - soft gray key (#F3F4F6 -> #E7E9EC), dark gray label
4. ghost     - no face at rest; faint gray fill on hover; a recessed well
               when pressed
5. text      - gray label with a thin underline and an arrow that nudges
               right on hover

Every filled variant is the same five material layers; only the values
change, so define them once as tokens and let each variant set its own:
1. Face: 180deg linear gradient, top 6-8% lighter than bottom.
2. Edge: 1px solid border one step darker than the bottom of the face
   (primary #12161F, secondary rgba(15,23,42,.14), tertiary rgba(15,23,42,.1)).
3. Top highlight: inset 0 1px 0 white (18% on slate, 85-100% on light
   faces). Put every inset layer in the button's own box-shadow, before the
   drop layers, never on a pseudo-element overlay: inset shadows on the
   element follow the inner radius (outer radius minus border), so the
   corners line up in every state.
4. Bottom shade: inset 0 -1px 0 black (22% on slate, 6% on light faces).
5. Drop shadow in two layers: a tight contact shadow 0 1px 2px plus a soft
   lift 0 4px 10px -3px (18% and 28% on slate, about a third of that on
   light faces).

States (hover, pressed/active, focus-visible, disabled):
- Hover: face one step lighter; the lift grows to 0 8px 16px -5px.
- Pressed: translateY(1px); flip the gradient (darker on top); the outer
  shadow collapses to 0 1px 1px; the top highlight becomes an inner shadow,
  inset 0 1px 2px black (40% on slate, 12-16% on light faces). Light faces
  keep a 1px white line below, 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.9), like a key
  pressed into paper.
- Give rest and pressed the same number of inset layers (pad with
  inset 0 0 0 transparent) so the shadow animates instead of jumping.
- Focus-visible and disabled follow the library's existing conventions.
- Timing: 120ms for transform, 140ms for shadows, 160ms for colors.

Sizes: all values above are for the 14px label size: height 40px,
padding 0 18px, radius 10px, label weight 600, optional 16px leading icon.
On the slate face add a label text-shadow 0 -1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.28).
Scale the material with the type, never keep it at fixed pixels: express
every length (height, padding, radius, border, icon, the 1px press offset,
and every shadow offset, blur and spread) as a multiple of a size unit
u = label size / 14. Provide two sizes: md (14px label, u = 1px) and
lg (16px label, u = 16/14 px, so height 45.7px, radius 11.4px, lift shadow
0 4.6px 11.4px -3.4px).

items.title: 少数人才知道的级联菜单小技巧：添加安全区域延时。
items.tip:
《999 个小技巧，让你 Vibe 的产品更有质感》

✨ 002 少数人才知道的级联菜单小技巧：添加安全区域延时。

什么是三角区？

 鼠标从父菜单斜着移向子菜单时，难免擦过下面几行。普通菜单一碰就切换，子菜单就“跑丢”了。

原理很简单：以鼠标上一刻的位置为顶点，连到子菜单靠近一侧的上下两个角，围成一个三角形。鼠标在三角形里，说明它正朝子菜单走，路过的行一律忽略；离开三角形，或者停留超过 1.2 秒，才切换到新的一行。

另外还有两个延时：悬停 220ms 后才打开子菜单；鼠标离开菜单 360ms 后才关闭。

prompts.text:
Define a cascading (nested) menu component that keeps its submenus steady: a safe zone plus three delays, so submenus open on purpose, survive diagonal moves toward them, and do not vanish on a brief slip out of the menu. If the project already has a menu or dropdown component, build this into its existing submenu logic and keep its API, keyboard support and accessibility as they are. Otherwise create one reusable CascadeMenu:

Props: an anchor (the trigger button that opens it on click) and a tree of items, each { label, icon?, href?, children? }. An item with children is a folder row; one without is a plain row that navigates on click.
Each level shows its folder's name as a small title above its rows.
Keyboard: arrow keys move through rows, Right/Enter opens a folder, Left goes back a level, Escape closes everything and returns focus to the anchor. Use menu / menuitem roles and aria-expanded on folder rows.
Behavior, with the values to use:

Open delay: hovering a row schedules it to take effect after 220ms: a folder row opens its submenu, a plain row closes any deeper submenu. Leaving the row before then cancels it. Touch input acts at once.
Safe zone: while a submenu is open, build a triangle from the pointer's previous position to the two corners of the submenu's near edge (the left edge's top and bottom for a submenu on the right). Track the last two pointermove positions and use the older one as the apex, so the triangle never collapses onto the current point. If the pointer is inside that triangle and within the parent's last min(90px, max(56px, 43% of the parent width)) toward the submenu, it is on its way there: rows it crosses must not highlight or open their own submenus.
Safe window: a row hovered inside the safe zone does not switch the submenu right away. Recheck every 80ms; switch once the pointer leaves the zone, or when 1200ms have passed since the hover began, so a pointer that simply stops there still gets its new submenu.
Close delay: when the pointer leaves the anchor, every open level and the safe zone, close the whole menu after 360ms. Coming back in time cancels the close. Clicking outside closes at once.
Dragging an item over a folder row opens it after 420ms instead of 220ms.
The pointer inside an open submenu ends all protection. Drive row highlight from component state (hovered, active, skipped), not from CSS :hover, or rows crossed inside the safe zone will still light up.
Geometry and motion:

Submenus open to the right, overlap their parent by 8px and align their first row with the parent row. Flip to the left when there is no room; the safe zone then uses the submenu's right edge.
Levels: 210-260px wide, sized to content, max height min(420px, 100vh - 24px) with their own scroll, 6px padding, 12px radius, 1px border, backdrop-filter blur(18px) saturate(135%).
Rows: 32px tall, 8px radius, 4px apart, 0 8px padding, 8px gap; 18px icon, 14px weight-500 label, a 16px chevron on folder rows. Level title: 11px, weight 600, quiet ink, padding 4px 8px 2px.
A submenu opens from its parent's edge: from translateX(-8px) scale(0.88, 0.98) and opacity 0, with opacity over 170ms and transform over 360ms on cubic-bezier(0.2, 1.45, 0.35, 1).
The root level opens the same way from its anchor: from translateY(-6px) scale(0.96, 0.86), top-left origin. Keep the overshoot curve: the slight spring is part of the feel.
A folder row's icon turns from a closed folder into an open one while its submenu is open, and back when it closes, over 460ms on cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1). Morph the paths if the two glyphs share their structure; otherwise cross-fade them with a slight lift of the front panel.
Light and dark themes come from tokens, not separate components:

Light: surface rgba(255,255,255,.96), border rgba(0,0,0,.14), row ink #263140, row hover rgba(15,23,42,.07), quiet ink #7A8491, chevron #94A3B8, shadow 0 18px 34px rgba(15,23,42,.12), 0 2px 4px rgba(15,23,42,.05), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.74).
Dark, neutral grays with no blue cast: surface rgba(34,34,34,.96), border rgba(255,255,255,.12), row ink #E4E4E4, row hover rgba(255,255,255,.08), quiet ink #9A9A9A, chevron #8A8A8A, shadow 0 18px 34px rgba(0,0,0,.42), 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,.2), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.06).
Monochrome brand icons invert in dark. Switching themes cross-fades colors, borders and shadows over about 500ms.
Keep every timing value as a named constant in one place, and keep the safe-zone math in a pure, unit-tested helper (point-in-triangle by the sign of the three edge cross products). Add an optional debug overlay that draws the zone (blue fill at 16%, dashed blue outline) and the running timer, off by default.

items.title: Dither 与 ASCII 参数化效果
items.tip:
新栏目《999 个小技巧，让你 Vibe 的产品更有质感》 

✨ 003 Dither 与 ASCII 参数化效果

001–003 都在我主页，关注我，每天一个让产品更有质感的小技巧

为你的登录页面/卡片添加可控的 Dither 与 ASCII 效果，并附带遮罩、色调、采样强度、大小、间距等可调参数。

两种效果怎么拆： 

ASCII：把画面切成网格，每格按亮度换成一个字符，从 “.” 到 “@” 越来越密。大小是字号，间距是格子疏密，采样强度是明暗对比，取样区域决定字画的是暗部还是亮部。 

Dither：把画面切成像素块，用 4×4 的 Bayer 矩阵当阈值，把每个颜色压成几级。大小是像素块，间距是纹理的尺度，采样强度越高，颜色级数越少，颗粒感越重。 两者都可以加一层遮罩，让画面退后，效果更像纹理而不是噪点。

推荐参数： 
ASCII：遮罩 90、取样暗部、采样强度 100、大小 37、间距 0 
Dither：遮罩 88、采样强度 100、大小 15、间距 0

prompts.text:
Add an ASCII / ordered-dither effect to one specific image or video in this project, with a live control panel next to it. Use the asset and the place I name (an , a , or a file path or URL, and the page or section it sits in); ask me if I have not named them. Apply the effect to that asset only, in place: keep its size, position, rounded corners and anything layered on top of it. If the project already has an image or canvas effect pipeline, or slider, segmented-control and panel components, build on them; otherwise create a reusable EffectLayer and EffectPanel.

Settings, one object shared by the layer and the panel: { filter: 'ascii' | 'dither', mask, palette, inkTone, strength, size, spacing } Keep separate values per filter, so switching filters brings back that filter's own settings.
What each control does in each filter, its range, and the recommended value (ASCII / Dither):

Mask effect, 0-100 (90 / 88): a vertical veil over the picture so the effect reads as texture rather than noise. Same in both filters.

Color, Original or one of five palettes (Original): gradient-maps the asset's luminance into one color family before filtering.
Sample tones, Shadows | Highlights (Shadows; ASCII only, hidden for Dither): which end of the tonal range becomes dense characters.
Sampling strength, 0-100 (100 / 100). ASCII: contrast of the tone curve and how bright and opaque the characters are. Dither: how few levels each color channel keeps (8 at 0, 2 at 100) and how fully the quantized color replaces the original.
Size, 0-100 (37 / 15). ASCII: font size, 7-24px. Dither: pixel block, 2-9px.
Spacing, 0-100 (0 / 0). ASCII: grid step, 8-24px across and 9-26px down, never tighter than the glyphs. Dither: scale of the Bayer pattern, 1-4 blocks per matrix cell.
Helpers used throughout:
range(v, a, b) = a + (b - a) * v / 100
luminance L = (0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B) / 255

s = strength / 100
"The box" is the asset's rendered size on the page.
Sampling:
Cover-fit the asset into the box and draw it into a small sampling canvas (about 480px on the long side), then read it with getImageData. A sample is the pixel under a point in the box, composited over white.
With a palette, recolor that canvas first: map each pixel's L through a 256-entry lookup built from the palette's four stops.

Per image or video frame, take about 12,000 evenly spaced samples: low = 8th percentile of L, high = 92nd percentile.
Shadows means dark ink, Highlights light ink.
ASCII:
Characters, from empty to full: " .,:;-=+xX08S#&@" (starts with two spaces).
Font: round(range(size, 7, 24))px monospace (22 instead of 24 when the box is under 720px wide), centered in each cell.

Grid: x step = max(range(spacing, 8, 24), widest glyph * 1.08); line height = max(range(spacing, 9, 26), height of "@" * 1.12, font * 1.04). The first cell sits half a step in from the edge.
Tone of a cell: raw = dark ink ? 1 - L : L; normalized = dark ink ? (high - L) / (high - low) : (L - low) / (high - low), clamped 0-1 (use raw alone when high - low < 0.025); mix = 0.72 + 0.14 s; t = raw (1 - mix) + normalized mix. Then a tone curve: black = 0.22 s, white = 1 - 0.08 s, lev = clamp((t - black) / (white - black), 0, 1), tone = lev (1 - s) + smoothstep(lev) s.
Skip cells with tone <= 0.02. Character = chars[round(tone * 16)]; skip spaces.
Ink: the sampled color lifted in HSV: value += (1 - value) * (0.24 + 0.18 s + 0.24 tone); saturation *= 1 + 0.16 + 0.2 s (clamped). Alpha = clamp((0.12 + 0.7 tone) (0.72 + 0.28 s), 0.06, 0.94).
Dither (ordered, Bayer 4x4):
pixel size = max(2, round(range(size, 2, 9))) (7 instead of 9 under 720px); pattern scale = max(1, round(range(spacing, 1, 4))); levels = max(2, round(range(strength, 8, 2))) per channel; blend = range(strength, 0.32, 1).
Matrix [[0,8,2,10],[12,4,14,6],[3,11,1,9],[15,7,13,5]]; threshold = (m + 0.5) / 16, indexed by floor(x / pattern scale), floor(y / pattern scale).

For each block sample its center, push saturation away from luma by 1 + 0.06 + 0.18 s, then per channel: scaled = c / 255 * (levels - 1); q = floor(scaled) + (fraction > threshold ? 1 : 0); out = c + (q / (levels - 1) * 255 - c) * blend.
Write the blocks into a canvas of box / pixel size and draw it scaled up with image smoothing off.
Mask and layering:
The mask is a vertical gradient with stops at the top, 42% and the bottom. Base opacities: on a light page white 54/20/38%, on a dark page black 44/20/50%. For a mask value v: stop = v <= 50 ? base * (v / 50)^1.08 : base + (100 - base) * ((v - 50) / 50)^1.08.
ASCII: draw the (recolored) picture, the mask, then the characters. Dither: draw the dithered picture, then the mask on top.

Changing filter or palette cross-fades from the last frame over 150ms.
Palettes (four stops at 0, 0.4, 0.74, 1):
meadow: #2B361F, #677D45, #AEBA78, #E5E1BD
blue: #192A4D, #326AC5, #A2C2F1, #EDF3FC
amber: #3C200F, #A74C15, #EF9A46, #F7E7CA
lavender: #292144, #6552AB, #B3A5E4, #F0ECFB

mono: #151515, #575757, #A6A6A6, #ECECEC
Rendering:
Draw into a canvas laid over the asset with the same size and corner radius, at devicePixelRatio capped at 1.6x and about 2048 x 2048.
Image: redraw when a setting changes (debounced 72ms).
Video: redraw on every new frame (requestVideoFrameCallback, falling back to requestAnimationFrame) while it plays and is on screen; keep the video element underneath as the source.
Control panel:

Place it next to the asset, below it when there is room, otherwise beside it, never covering it. About 420px wide, centered on the asset.
Rows, in order: Mask effect, Filter (two tabs: ASCII | Dither), Color (round swatches), Sample tones (ASCII only), Sampling strength, Size, Spacing (shown with %).
Each row 46px tall: a 136px label column, then the control. Slider: a 22px track with 8px radius and a filled part, a 9x30 rounded-rectangle thumb (3px radius), a number box with the value centered, and a snap mark at 50. Swatches: 22px circles, each filled with its palette's two middle stops at 135deg (Original: a tiny crop of the asset); the selected one gets a ring with a small gap.
Every change applies live while dragging. Add a "Reset to recommended" action that restores the values above for the current filter.

Follow the page's light or dark theme and the project's tokens.

Cover-fit the asset into the box and draw it into a small sampling canvas (about 480px on the long side), then read it with getImageData. A sample is the pixel under a point in the box, composited over white.
With a palette, recolor that canvas first: map each pixel's L through a 256-entry lookup built from the palette's four stops.

Per image or video frame, take about 12,000 evenly spaced samples: low = 8th percentile of L, high = 92nd percentile.
Shadows means dark ink, Highlights light ink.
ASCII:
Characters, from empty to full: " .,:;-=+xX08S#&@" (starts with two spaces).
Font: round(range(size, 7, 24))px monospace (22 instead of 24 when the box is under 720px wide), centered in each cell.

Grid: x step = max(range(spacing, 8, 24), widest glyph * 1.08); line height = max(range(spacing, 9, 26), height of "@" * 1.12, font * 1.04). The first cell sits half a step in from the edge.
Tone of a cell: raw = dark ink ? 1 - L : L; normalized = dark ink ? (high - L) / (high - low) : (L - low) / (high - low), clamped 0-1 (use raw alone when high - low < 0.025); mix = 0.72 + 0.14 s; t = raw (1 - mix) + normalized mix. Then a tone curve: black = 0.22 s, white = 1 - 0.08 s, lev = clamp((t - black) / (white - black), 0, 1), tone = lev (1 - s) + smoothstep(lev) s.
Skip cells with tone <= 0.02. Character = chars[round(tone * 16)]; skip spaces.
Ink: the sampled color lifted in HSV: value += (1 - value) * (0.24 + 0.18 s + 0.24 tone); saturation *= 1 + 0.16 + 0.2 s (clamped). Alpha = clamp((0.12 + 0.7 tone) (0.72 + 0.28 s), 0.06, 0.94).
Dither (ordered, Bayer 4x4):
pixel size = max(2, round(range(size, 2, 9))) (7 instead of 9 under 720px); pattern scale = max(1, round(range(spacing, 1, 4))); levels = max(2, round(range(strength, 8, 2))) per channel; blend = range(strength, 0.32, 1).
Matrix [[0,8,2,10],[12,4,14,6],[3,11,1,9],[15,7,13,5]]; threshold = (m + 0.5) / 16, indexed by floor(x / pattern scale), floor(y / pattern scale).

For each block sample its center, push saturation away from luma by 1 + 0.06 + 0.18 s, then per channel: scaled = c / 255 * (levels - 1); q = floor(scaled) + (fraction > threshold ? 1 : 0); out = c + (q / (levels - 1) * 255 - c) * blend.
Write the blocks into a canvas of box / pixel size and draw it scaled up with image smoothing off.
Mask and layering:
The mask is a vertical gradient with stops at the top, 42% and the bottom. Base opacities: on a light page white 54/20/38%, on a dark page black 44/20/50%. For a mask value v: stop = v <= 50 ? base * (v / 50)^1.08 : base + (100 - base) * ((v - 50) / 50)^1.08.
ASCII: draw the (recolored) picture, the mask, then the characters. Dither: draw the dithered picture, then the mask on top.

Changing filter or palette cross-fades from the last frame over 150ms.
Palettes (four stops at 0, 0.4, 0.74, 1):
meadow: #2B361F, #677D45, #AEBA78, #E5E1BD
blue: #192A4D, #326AC5, #A2C2F1, #EDF3FC
amber: #3C200F, #A74C15, #EF9A46, #F7E7CA
lavender: #292144, #6552AB, #B3A5E4, #F0ECFB

mono: #151515, #575757, #A6A6A6, #ECECEC
Rendering:
Draw into a canvas laid over the asset with the same size and corner radius, at devicePixelRatio capped at 1.6x and about 2048 x 2048.
Image: redraw when a setting changes (debounced 72ms).
Video: redraw on every new frame (requestVideoFrameCallback, falling back to requestAnimationFrame) while it plays and is on screen; keep the video element underneath as the source.
Control panel:

Place it next to the asset, below it when there is room, otherwise beside it, never covering it. About 420px wide, centered on the asset.
Rows, in order: Mask effect, Filter (two tabs: ASCII | Dither), Color (round swatches), Sample tones (ASCII only), Sampling strength, Size, Spacing (shown with %).
Each row 46px tall: a 136px label column, then the control. Slider: a 22px track with 8px radius and a filled part, a 9x30 rounded-rectangle thumb (3px radius), a number box with the value centered, and a snap mark at 50. Swatches: 22px circles, each filled with its palette's two middle stops at 135deg (Original: a tiny crop of the asset); the selected one gets a ring with a small gap.
Every change applies live while dragging. Add a "Reset to recommended" action that restores the values above for the current filter.

Follow the page's light or dark theme and the project's tokens.

items.title: 使用递进式圆角数值 + 连续曲率圆角（超椭圆）
items.tip:
新栏目《999 个小技巧，让你 Vibe 的产品更有质感》

✨ 004 使用递进式圆角数值 + 连续曲率圆角（超椭圆）

001–004 都在我主页，关注我，每天一个让产品更有质感的小技巧

👉要点一：等距内缩。当你想让表单、嵌套卡片的各种元素看起来更规整的时候，使用递进式圆角。保证每一层都遵守：

内圆角 = 外圆角 − 间距，内外共用一个圆心

👉要点二：连续圆角/超椭圆。普通圆角接直边的地方有一道折痕，连续圆角过渡更顺（类比 iOS）： 

border-radius: 32px
corner-shape: superellipse(1.25)

Chrome / Edge 139+ 支持；Safari、Firefox 暂不支持，会自动退回普通圆角。

prompts.text:
Make the corner radii in this UI consistent, then switch them to continuous corners. Work on the screen or components I name; ask me if I have not named them. If the project has radius tokens, change those instead of hard-coding values.

Inner radius = outer radius - padding (r = R - p)
Go from the outside in: dialog or card -> panels, inputs, buttons -> chips and tags. A box p inside a container with radius R gets R - p, so both corners share one center. Example: dialog 32, padding 16 -> panels and buttons 16; a chip 8 inside a 16 panel -> 8.
Boxes on the same level share one radius. Never go below 4.

Pills and circles stay fully round.
Keep every padding, gap and radius on a 4px grid.
Continuous corners
Keep border-radius and add the curve as progressive enhancement: @ supports (corner-shape: superellipse(1.25)) { :where(*) { corner-shape: superellipse(1.25); } } Set corner-shape: round on pills and circles.

Chrome and Edge 139+ render it; Safari and Firefox skip the block and show the plain border-radius.
When done, list every radius you changed as "element: old -> new".

items.title: 更灵动的拖拽排序
items.tip:
新栏目《999 个小技巧，让你 Vibe 的产品更有质感》
001–005 都在我主页，关注我，每天一个让产品更有质感的小技巧

✨ 005 更灵动的拖拽排序

做横向或纵向的拖拽排序时，让落点两侧的元素轻轻让开，并且由近及远依次启动，动作会更像真实世界里的推挤。

prompts.text:
要点：
1. 光标及时反馈：悬停时变成手指，按下时变成抓手；
2. 落点用一条插入线提示：出现时从中间轻轻展开，拖动时跟着移到新的落点；
3. 插入线两侧的元素向外避让，离得越近，让得越多、动得越早：
位移 = 10px × 0.7ⁿ
延迟 = 24ms × n
（n 是与插入线相隔的层数，紧挨着的为 0）

可以直接喂给 AI 的部分：

Make drag-to-reorder in my product feel like this. Apply it to the lists,
rows and docks I name, and reuse any drag helper the project already has.

1. Cursor: a pointing hand over anything draggable, a grabbing hand while
   dragging.
2. Lift: the picked item follows the pointer, raised off the list so it
   never hides where it will land: above a horizontal row, or pulled aside
   and shrunk to about 90% in a vertical list. Its old slot closes up.
3. Drop hint: a faint, thin line in the gap where it will land (vertical in
   a row, horizontal in a list), about 15% of the text color. It grows from
   its middle when it appears and glides to each new gap. No line over the
   item's own slot.
4. Ripple: items on both sides of the line lean away from it. Counting n
   from the line (0 = the item touching it), item n moves
   A x 0.7^n (A is about 10px for icons, 8px for cards)
   and starts 24ms x n later, on a quick spring that barely overshoots and
   settles in about 0.25s. Nearer items move sooner and further, so the
   push spreads out like a ripple.
5. Drop: the item takes the gap and every item springs into its new place.
   Escape or dropping outside the list cancels, and everything springs back.
6. Give each motion its own curve (hand-like for the pointer, a small pop
   for the lift, springs for settling) instead of one ease-out everywhere.

Move things with transforms, not layout. Let the keyboard reorder too, and
with reduced motion keep only the line.

items.title: 像书一样翻开的卡片
items.tip:
新栏目《999 个小技巧，让你 Vibe 的产品更有质感》

✨ 006 像书一样翻开的卡片

001–005 都在我主页，关注我，每天一个让产品更有质感的小技巧

prompts.text:
Vibe 出来的产品，最容易撞脸的就是卡片。不如让卡片平时保持原样，悬停时像一本小书一样翻开一点，露出里面的几页。

同一套动效，三种风格：Default（普通产品卡片）、Skeuomorphic（拟物精装书）、Minimal（极简文档册）。

要点：
1. 卡片由封面、4 页内页和封底叠成，绕左边翻开；平时完全重合，看起来就是一张普通卡片；
2. 封面翻得最多，越往里翻得越少、动得越晚，移开时倒序合上：角度 = 42° × 0.7ⁿ，延迟 = 28ms × n
3. 光从上方来：阴影是实心的两层，翻开时往下拉长、变柔；前一页给后一页投下阴影，直到两页分开。

Make the cards in my product open a little, like a book, when hovered.
At rest a card must look exactly as it does today; only hover or focus
reveals that it is a small book with pages inside.

## 0. Start from what exists
- Find the card component I name (or the one used in the grid or list I
  point to) and retrofit it in place. Reuse its markup, design tokens,
  radius, shadow and motion or spring utilities.
- Keep the card's footprint, padding, content and layout unchanged.
  Nothing around the card may move.
- If I ask for new cards instead, build a fresh square card (about
  280 x 280) in the style I choose below.
- Any option I leave unset uses the default marked *.

## 1. Choose a style
Default*: ordinary product cards, identical to normal ones until hovered.
- Surface: plain white (or my card surface token), no texture.
- Edge: a 1px hairline in my border colour.
- Shadow: light, neutral cool grey, half strength.
- Type: the product sans. Title 24/600, description 15 muted,
  meta 14 muted.
- Cover: the existing card UI: a 48px icon tile, a ↗ arrow top right,
  title, description, and a meta footer below a hairline.
- Wall: my normal page background.
- Pages: white, a faint shade toward the spine, a small heading and
  4-6 grey text lines.

Skeuomorphic: hardcover books on a gallery wall.
- Surface: fine bookcloth grain over a deep cover colour.
- Edge: a lit bevel: bright top edge, darker foot.
- Shadow: warm, near-neutral grey (never orange), full strength.
- Type: one serif title, bottom left. Nothing else on the cover.
- Cover: a full-bleed image or animated ASCII scene, with a soft gloss
  at the top and shade at the foot.
- Wall: warm plaster with a fine grain and a spotlight over each book.
- Pages: cream paper with grain, an italic chapter heading, justified
  lines, and thin page edges along the fore-edge.

Minimal: documentation volumes.
- Surface: flat off-white, light grey or graphite, one tone per card.
- Edge: a faint bevel or hairline.
- Shadow: cool neutral grey.
- Type: a mono section number and version on top, over a hairline rule;
  a two-line sans title and a small grey label at the foot.
- Cover: one small grey line diagram with a single element in the ink
  colour.
- Wall: cool grey with a faint 24px dot grid and soft light from above.
- Pages: cool white, a sans heading and grey lines.

Match my product: take surface, edge, shadow, type and wall from my
tokens, and keep the cover exactly as the card is today.

## 2. Options (defaults marked *)
- Intensity: subtle (A = 24deg) | book* (A = 42deg) | dramatic
  (A = 60deg).
- Pages: 2 | 3 | 4* | 6.
- Hinge: left* | right | top.
- Trigger: hover* | press (open while pressed) | scroll into view (open
  once when 60% visible, close after ~1.2s). Keyboard focus always
  opens it too.
- Pages show: blank paper | lines of text* | real preview content from
  the card (its next fields, a short list, a chart thumbnail).
- Cover: existing card UI* | image | animated ASCII scene | solid colour.
- Shadow direction: from above* | from top-left.
- Shadow strength: none | light | normal* | deep.
- Corners: match my tokens* | continuous (superellipse).
- Motion feel: snappy (k 320, damping 0.9) | default* (k 240,
  damping 0.86) | soft (k 160, damping 0.8). All barely overshoot.
- Reduced motion: tiny lift* | nothing.
- Touch: press* | scroll into view | off.

## 3. Layer stack
- Inside the card's link, put the cover on a body element with
  transform-style: preserve-3d. Behind it stack N pages and a back
  board, all absolutely positioned on the same square.
- Order, front to back: cover (n = 0), pages (n = 1..N), back board
  (n = N + 1, never moves).
- The cover keeps all of the card's existing content. Pages and the
  back board are decorative: aria-hidden, no links, no tab stops.
- Perspective on the static outer element: about 1100px, origin toward
  the hinge (30% 50% for left, 70% 50% for right, 50% 30% for top).
- transform-origin on the hinge edge of every layer: left 0 50%,
  right 100% 50%, top 50% 0. backface-visibility: hidden.
- Lift layer n by translateZ((N + 1 - n) x 0.6px) so layers never
  fight in depth.
- Pages sit 8px inside the cover (4px at the spine), like a book block,
  with radius = cover radius - 8.
- Back board: on flat cards (Default, Minimal) inset it ~6px from the
  cover with radius = cover radius - 6, so it never peeks out past the
  cover's foreshortened corners. On Skeuomorphic it is flush, the cover
  colour darkened ~28%.

## 4. Motion
- Layer n turns toward the viewer by
    angle(n) = A x 0.7^n
  and starts
    delay(n) = 28ms x n
  later. The cover leads; pages fan out behind it.
- Direction: rotateY(-angle) for a left hinge, rotateY(+angle) for
  right, rotateX(+angle) for top.
- Each layer runs on its own spring (see Motion feel), settling in
  about 0.3s.
- Close in reverse: the innermost page first, delay = 28ms x (N - n),
  back to 0deg.
- If the pointer leaves mid-way, retarget from the current angle and
  velocity. Never jump.
- No spring helper in the project? CSS transitions are fine: transition
  transform over ~420ms with a slight overshoot, e.g.
  cubic-bezier(0.3, 1.2, 0.5, 1), and set transition-delay to 28ms x n
  in the open state and 28ms x (N - n) at rest (the target state's delay
  applies, so closing runs in reverse).

## 5. Light and shading
- Light comes from above, so the shadow falls down the wall.
- The shadow is two solid shapes behind the card, each blurred once.
  At rest it hugs the card like any flat card's:
  - contact: small and darker, at the foot. Lower half of the card,
    ~4px in from each side, blur ~4px, ~2px down, ~22% opacity.
  - ambient: faint. Blur ~14px, ~6px down, ~12% opacity.
- Never a box-shadow: it is a hollow ring and shows as an outline once
  the cover swings off it.
- Tint: near-neutral grey nudged toward the wall (warm grey on a warm
  wall, cool grey on a cool one). Never pure black, never saturated.
- Strength scales both opacities: light 0.5 (Default style), normal 1,
  deep 1.4.
- Opening: crossfade to a second pre-blurred pair that is longer and
  softer (contact blur ~12px, 12px down; ambient blur ~38px, 26px down),
  and move it ~14px further down and ~4% wider with transform. Drive it
  with one progress value o (0..1) on its own spring (k 200, damping
  0.9): rest pair opacity 1 - o, open pair opacity o.
- Leaf shading: every page has an overlay gradient from the spine
  (32% dark -> 8% at 55% -> 0 at 85%). Its opacity is
    clamp(gap / 6, 0, 1) x max(0, 1 - gap / 30)
  where gap = the angle of the leaf in front minus this leaf's angle.
  A page is shaded while the leaf in front is just lifting off it, then
  lit once they part.
- Covers (Skeuomorphic, Minimal): a soft gloss at the top edge and a
  little shade at the foot.

## 6. Corners and edges
- Clip every layer (cover, pages, back board) to one shape path, and
  draw its edge (hairline or bevel) along that exact path, e.g. an SVG
  path stroked over the layer. Do not mix a CSS border or inset
  box-shadow with the clip: they disagree at the corners and show a
  second rim when the layers part.
- Match my tokens: use the token radius; nested radius = outer - inset.
- Continuous: superellipse corners |x|^n + |y|^n = 1 with n = 2^1.25
  (the same curve as CSS corner-shape: superellipse(1.25)). Generate a
  clip-path: path(...) per layer size, reuse it for the edge, and
  regenerate on resize.

## 7. Interaction and accessibility
- Hit-test on the resting footprint: listen for hover on the static
  outer element and give every moving layer pointer-events: none, so a
  swinging cover never moves the target and the card never flickers
  open and closed at its edges.
- Cursor: a pointing hand over the whole card.
- The whole card stays one <a> or <button> with its current accessible
  name. Pages add nothing to the accessibility tree.
- :focus-visible opens it exactly like hover. Keep the focus ring on the
  outer element, along the resting shape.
- Reduced motion: no fan and no rotation. The cover lifts ~2px and the
  shadow crossfades to the open pair.
- Touch: no hover. Use the Touch option; a tap must still activate the
  card on the first try.

## 8. Performance
- Animate transform and opacity only. Never animate blur, box-shadow,
  clip-path, width, height or top/left.
- Never animate a blur radius: blur each shadow once and crossfade the
  two pre-blurred versions.
- One requestAnimationFrame loop for all cards. Skip cards whose springs
  are at rest, and stop the loop when nothing moves.
- Write a style only when its value changes (cache the last string per
  element).
- No layout reads per frame: measure once, and again on resize
  (ResizeObserver).
- Animated canvas ∂∂: draw at ~30fps at most, and pause when off
  screen (IntersectionObserver) or when the tab is hidden.

## 9. Animated ASCII cover (only if chosen)
- Paint a small scene as one colour per character cell (~6 x 9px).
- Pick each character by brightness from " .:-=+*#%@".
- Draw a dimmed copy of the colours (~40%) underneath and the coloured
  characters on top, so the gaps read like a halftone.
- Stamp characters from a pre-rendered glyph atlas instead of laying out
  text every frame. Keep the motion slow and seamlessly looping.

## 10. When done
- List every file you changed or added.
- List the style and every option you used, marking which were
  defaults.
- Note anything that no longer looks identical at rest.

- Type: a mono section number and version on top, over a hairline rule;
  a two-line sans title and a small grey label at the foot.
- Cover: one small grey line diagram with a single element in the ink
  colour.
- Wall: cool grey with a faint 24px dot grid and soft light from above.
- Pages: cool white, a sans heading and grey lines.

Match my product: take surface, edge, shadow, type and wall from my
tokens, and keep the cover exactly as the card is today.

## 2. Options (defaults marked *)
- Intensity: subtle (A = 24deg) | book* (A = 42deg) | dramatic
  (A = 60deg).
- Pages: 2 | 3 | 4* | 6.
- Hinge: left* | right | top.
- Trigger: hover* | press (open while pressed) | scroll into view (open
  once when 60% visible, close after ~1.2s). Keyboard focus always
  opens it too.
- Pages show: blank paper | lines of text* | real preview content from
  the card (its next fields, a short list, a chart thumbnail).
- Cover: existing card UI* | image | animated ASCII scene | solid colour.
- Shadow direction: from above* | from top-left.
- Shadow strength: none | light | normal* | deep.
- Corners: match my tokens* | continuous (superellipse).
- Motion feel: snappy (k 320, damping 0.9) | default* (k 240,
  damping 0.86) | soft (k 160, damping 0.8). All barely overshoot.
- Reduced motion: tiny lift* | nothing.
- Touch: press* | scroll into view | off.

## 3. Layer stack
- Inside the card's link, put the cover on a body element with
  transform-style: preserve-3d. Behind it stack N pages and a back
  board, all absolutely positioned on the same square.
- Order, front to back: cover (n = 0), pages (n = 1..N), back board
  (n = N + 1, never moves).
- The cover keeps all of the card's existing content. Pages and the
  back board are decorative: aria-hidden, no links, no tab stops.
- Perspective on the static outer element: about 1100px, origin toward
  the hinge (30% 50% for left, 70% 50% for right, 50% 30% for top).
- transform-origin on the hinge edge of every layer: left 0 50%,
  right 100% 50%, top 50% 0. backface-visibility: hidden.
- Lift layer n by translateZ((N + 1 - n) x 0.6px) so layers never
  fight in depth.
- Pages sit 8px inside the cover (4px at the spine), like a book block,
  with radius = cover radius - 8.
- Back board: on flat cards (Default, Minimal) inset it ~6px from the
  cover with radius = cover radius - 6, so it never peeks out past the
  cover's foreshortened corners. On Skeuomorphic it is flush, the cover
  colour darkened ~28%.

## 4. Motion
- Layer n turns toward the viewer by
    angle(n) = A x 0.7^n
  and starts
    delay(n) = 28ms x n
  later. The cover leads; pages fan out behind it.
- Direction: rotateY(-angle) for a left hinge, rotateY(+angle) for
  right, rotateX(+angle) for top.
- Each layer runs on its own spring (see Motion feel), settling in
  about 0.3s.
- Close in reverse: the innermost page first, delay = 28ms x (N - n),
  back to 0deg.
- If the pointer leaves mid-way, retarget from the current angle and
  velocity. Never jump.
- No spring helper in the project? CSS transitions are fine: transition
  transform over ~420ms with a slight overshoot, e.g.
  cubic-bezier(0.3, 1.2, 0.5, 1), and set transition-delay to 28ms x n
  in the open state and 28ms x (N - n) at rest (the target state's delay
  applies, so closing runs in reverse).

## 5. Light and shading
- Light comes from above, so the shadow falls down the wall.
- The shadow is two solid shapes behind the card, each blurred once.
  At rest it hugs the card like any flat card's:
  - contact: small and darker, at the foot. Lower half of the card,
    ~4px in from each side, blur ~4px, ~2px down, ~22% opacity.
  - ambient: faint. Blur ~14px, ~6px down, ~12% opacity.
- Never a box-shadow: it is a hollow ring and shows as an outline once
  the cover swings off it.
- Tint: near-neutral grey nudged toward the wall (warm grey on a warm
  wall, cool grey on a cool one). Never pure black, never saturated.
- Strength scales both opacities: light 0.5 (Default style), normal 1,
  deep 1.4.
- Opening: crossfade to a second pre-blurred pair that is longer and
  softer (contact blur ~12px, 12px down; ambient blur ~38px, 26px down),
  and move it ~14px further down and ~4% wider with transform. Drive it
  with one progress value o (0..1) on its own spring (k 200, damping
  0.9): rest pair opacity 1 - o, open pair opacity o.
- Leaf shading: every page has an overlay gradient from the spine
  (32% dark -> 8% at 55% -> 0 at 85%). Its opacity is
    clamp(gap / 6, 0, 1) x max(0, 1 - gap / 30)
  where gap = the angle of the leaf in front minus this leaf's angle.
  A page is shaded while the leaf in front is just lifting off it, then
  lit once they part.
- Covers (Skeuomorphic, Minimal): a soft gloss at the top edge and a
  little shade at the foot.

## 6. Corners and edges
- Clip every layer (cover, pages, back board) to one shape path, and
  draw its edge (hairline or bevel) along that exact path, e.g. an SVG
  path stroked over the layer. Do not mix a CSS border or inset
  box-shadow with the clip: they disagree at the corners and show a
  second rim when the layers part.
- Match my tokens: use the token radius; nested radius = outer - inset.
- Continuous: superellipse corners |x|^n + |y|^n = 1 with n = 2^1.25
  (the same curve as CSS corner-shape: superellipse(1.25)). Generate a
  clip-path: path(...) per layer size, reuse it for the edge, and
  regenerate on resize.

## 7. Interaction and accessibility
- Hit-test on the resting footprint: listen for hover on the static
  outer element and give every moving layer pointer-events: none, so a
  swinging cover never moves the target and the card never flickers
  open and closed at its edges.
- Cursor: a pointing hand over the whole card.
- The whole card stays one <a> or <button> with its current accessible
  name. Pages add nothing to the accessibility tree.
- :focus-visible opens it exactly like hover. Keep the focus ring on the
  outer element, along the resting shape.
- Reduced motion: no fan and no rotation. The cover lifts ~2px and the
  shadow crossfades to the open pair.
- Touch: no hover. Use the Touch option; a tap must still activate the
  card on the first try.

## 8. Performance
- Animate transform and opacity only. Never animate blur, box-shadow,
  clip-path, width, height or top/left.
- Never animate a blur radius: blur each shadow once and crossfade the
  two pre-blurred versions.
- One requestAnimationFrame loop for all cards. Skip cards whose springs
  are at rest, and stop the loop when nothing moves.
- Write a style only when its value changes (cache the last string per
  element).
- No layout reads per frame: measure once, and again on resize
  (ResizeObserver).
- Animated canvas ∂∂: draw at ~30fps at most, and pause when off
  screen (IntersectionObserver) or when the tab is hidden.

## 9. Animated ASCII cover (only if chosen)
- Paint a small scene as one colour per character cell (~6 x 9px).
- Pick each character by brightness from " .:-=+*#%@".
- Draw a dimmed copy of the colours (~40%) underneath and the coloured
  characters on top, so the gaps read like a halftone.
- Stamp characters from a pre-rendered glyph atlas instead of laying out
  text every frame. Keep the motion slow and seamlessly looping.

## 10. When done
- List every file you changed or added.
- List the style and every option you used, marking which were
  defaults.
- Note anything that no longer looks identical at rest.

prompts.text:
Polish the typography in my product with a set of CSS switches. Change only how text wraps, spaces, aligns and truncates. No copy, font, colour or layout changes beyond what each rule says.

0. Start from what exists
- Put the rules in the global text styles (base CSS, typography tokens, Tailwind config or shared text components) so every page inherits them. Add per-component rules only where a component overrides the base.
- Every rule below is progressive enhancement: browsers that don't know a property ignore it. Add no polyfills.
- Scope the Chinese rules with :lang(zh), and make sure the lang attribute is set on the html element or on the element itself, so English text keeps its own rules.

1. Headings break into even lines
- On h1 to h3, card titles and hero lines: text-wrap: balance;
- Lines come out about the same length, so a heading never ends on one lonely word. Short text only: Chrome balances up to 6 lines.

2. No lone word at the end of a paragraph
- On paragraphs, descriptions and list items: text-wrap: pretty;
- Also join pairs that must not split with a non-breaking space (U+00A0): an em dash and the name after it, a number and its unit.

3. Numbers that change keep their width
- On anything that updates in place or sits in a column (counters, prices, timers, stats, table cells): font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
- The font must have tabular figures (the tnum feature); check that the width actually stops changing. Leave running text proportional.

4. Button labels stay on one line
- On buttons and other labels in flex rows: white-space: nowrap; (flex-shrink: 0 works too)
- A crowded row must not squeeze a label onto two lines.

5. Long text truncates instead of spilling out
- A flex item won't shrink below its content, so text inside it can't truncate. On the flex item: min-width: 0;
- On the text itself: overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis;
- When the text really is cut (scrollWidth > clientWidth), show the full text in a tooltip on hover.

6. Chinese body text: justified, on a whole number of characters
- On Chinese paragraphs only: text-align: justify;
- Set the measure to a whole number of characters (for example max-width: 26em at the paragraph's font size), so a justified line only stretches to absorb Latin words and squeezed punctuation.
- Not for narrow columns (under about 15 characters), short text, captions, buttons or mostly-English text: the gaps get uneven.

7. Space between Chinese and Latin text or numbers
- On Chinese text: text-autospace: normal;
- The browser adds a thin gap between Han characters and Latin letters or digits. Don't also hand-type spaces in copy or translation files. Skip code, inputs and monospaced text.

8. No half-width gap before an opening bracket at a line start
- On Chinese UI text without a first-line indent: text-spacing-trim: trim-start;
- An opening 「 “ （ at the start of a line drops its blank half and lines up with the text above. Long-form text with a two-character indent should use space-first instead. Chrome only for now.

9. Chinese headings break between words
- Chinese has no spaces, so a heading can split a word across lines. Mark the break points between words with BudouX (its Simplified or Traditional Chinese model), inserting a wbr element at each one, at build time for static copy or at render time for dynamic copy. Then: word-break: keep-all; overflow-wrap: anywhere; text-wrap: balance;
- Never use keep-all on Chinese without break points: the heading becomes one unbreakable word. Don't use Intl.Segmenter for this (it splits common words wrongly), and don't apply it to body text.

10. Line-start and line-end rules (避头尾)
- Browsers already keep punctuation off the start of a line and squeeze line-end punctuation. Don't rebuild this.
- Find and remove any line-break: anywhere used to stop overflow: it turns these rules off. Use overflow-wrap: anywhere instead.
- Text drawn on canvas or SVG, or wrapped by hand in JS, gets none of this: apply the rules there yourself.

11. When done
- List every file and selector you changed.
- List every line-break: anywhere and word-break: break-all you removed or kept, and why.
- Show before and after on my own pages: a wrapped heading, a paragraph ending, a changing number, a truncated label and a mixed Chinese-English paragraph.

items.title: 如何设计 Wiki 的框架和布局，兼顾 PC 和移动端体验？
items.tip:
日更栏目-《999 个小技巧，让你 Vibe 的产品更有质感》

✨ 008 如何设计 Wiki 的框架和布局，兼顾 PC 和移动端体验？

当产品开始变复杂，或者官网需要写大量 SEO 文章时，一套可靠的 Wiki 页面既能快速解答用户疑问，也能带来 SEO 流量。

那么：
Q1：移动端怎么优雅地切换章节？
Q2：章节导航太多，超出一屏怎么办？
Q3：文末引导有什么意义？
Q4：Footer 为什么应该超过半屏高？
Q5：导航栏的信息结构怎么安排？

A1：移动端以直板机为主，屏幕大多较窄。可以在底部常驻一个菜单栏，点开后用满屏菜单展示章节。一行一个，方便点击。

A2：导航用独立高度，和正文分开，超出部分上下截断。截断的边缘务必加渐变遮罩，让用户知道上下还有内容；再配一个居中的箭头按钮，便于点击。

A3：不管是人还是 AI 来读，在一篇解答问题的文章下面附上社群、社媒账号按钮，都能快速带来转化。卡片样式记得贴近正文组件，看起来更原生。这相当于为你的转化目标免费投了一则“上下文广告”。

A4：用好看的背景图撑高页脚，吸引用户滑到底并停留。再放上足够有用的信息，真正帮用户解决问题，才不会招人反感。

A5：LOGO（返回官网）+ 关键页面下拉菜单 + 核心 CTA 按钮，滚动时保持吸顶。注意 Safari 等浏览器会根据导航栏颜色给地址栏着色，导航栏背景色要和品牌协调。

001–008 都在主页，关注我，每天一个让产品更有质感的小技巧。

🎉 下一期你想看什么？欢迎友好讨论。

prompts.text:
Polish the layout of my docs or help center pages: the header, the page list, the outline and the end of each article. Keep the content, copy, colours and fonts. Change only how these parts sit, scroll and respond.

0. Start from what exists
- Find the shared docs layout, the site header, the page list (sidebar), the outline (table of contents) and the footer. Change those, so every page inherits the result.
- Use CSS and a little plain JS. Add no scroll or animation libraries.

1. Think of the page as three layers
- The article and the footer scroll with the page.
- The page list and the outline are position: sticky. They stop where they start, so they never jump when scrolling begins, and the end of the layout pushes them up at the bottom.
- The header becomes position: fixed only after the page's opening (banner or hero) has left the screen. Before that it belongs to the page and scrolls away with it.

2. Header: it scrolls away, then comes back floating
- At the top it is clear, with no background.
- Once the reader has scrolled and the banner's bottom edge is at or above the top of the screen (getBoundingClientRect().bottom <= 0), show it as a floating bar: position: fixed; a translucent white background; backdrop-filter: blur(18px); a soft shadow.
- It enters in 320ms ease-out, from translateY(-24px) with blur(8px) and opacity 0. It leaves in 120ms when the reader scrolls back up to the banner. If the reader scrolls down again during the exit, cancel it and keep the bar.
- Give headings a scroll-margin-top so anchor links never land under the bar.

3. Page list: it scrolls on its own, and shows where there is more
- Hide its scrollbar and let it scroll by itself.
- Fade an edge only while more of the list waits beyond it. Toggle data-more-above and data-more-below on scroll and resize, and drive a mask-image: linear-gradient(...) with them: about 40px at the top and 56px at the bottom, each with a short fully clear strip at the very edge, so a half-cut row never shows as a faint line.
- Add a small round arrow on each edge that has more. A click scrolls the list by 60% of its visible height, smoothly. Arrows are for the mouse only (tabindex="-1", aria-hidden="true"); keyboard focus already scrolls the list.
- On load, bring the current page into view. Keep the list's scroll position in sessionStorage, so moving to another page does not reset it.
- If there is a search box, let "/" focus it.

4. Outline: mark the section being read
- The current section is the last heading above a line 20% down the viewport.
- Mark its link with aria-current="location" and style that: border-left-color and text in the accent colour.
- Update it on scroll, at most once per animation frame.

5. End of the article: help first, then the next page
- If the reader is still stuck, a "Still need help?" card with one or two real channels (the issue tracker, the community, a contact).
- Then previous and next links, with each page's title. The first page links back to the home page.
- Then the footer.

6. Narrow screens
- Hide the outline on tablets and the page list on phones. Put both in one bar fixed at the bottom: the page list on its left half, the outline on its right half.
- The right half shows the name of the section being read, updated by the same 20% line, and truncated with an ellipsis when it is long.
- A tap on either half opens its list as a sheet from the bottom edge (a dialog opened with showModal()), sliding up 24px as it fades in, with no dimming behind it. Mark the current entry and scroll it into view (scrollIntoView({ block: "center" })).
- A tap on an entry, the close button, outside the sheet or Esc closes it; a section link then scrolls to its heading.
- Make the tap targets one size up from the desktop list.

7. Motion
- Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, turn off smooth scrolling and the header's enter and exit animations.

8. When done
- List every file and selector you changed.
- Check four states on my own pages: the top of a page, the middle, the end, and a phone-width window.
- Show a screenshot of each.

items.title: 提示框、跟随气泡、就地确认、抽屉与弹窗，到底怎么选？
items.tip:
日更栏目《999 个小技巧，让你 Vibe 的产品更有质感》

✨ 009 提示框、跟随气泡、就地确认、抽屉与弹窗，到底怎么选？

Q1：提示框和跟随气泡，区别在哪？
Q2：操作要让用户确认，怎样才不打扰？
Q3：表单该放进弹窗、抽屉，还是单独一页？

1️⃣
提示框（Tooltip）为光标所指的内容补充文字，常见于被折叠的长文本；要放操作，就改用点击打开的气泡（Popover）。

2️⃣
能撤销的操作，直接执行，再留一个「撤销」入口。

3️⃣
表单短、不需要参照界面上的其他信息，用弹窗；
表单长、需要对照界面内容，或想更好地利用横向空间，用抽屉；

Review how my product uses floating UI (tooltips, tooltips that follow the pointer, popovers, popconfirms, drawers and dialogs) and decide which kind each case should be. 1. What each kind is for
- Tooltip: adds text about what the pointer is on, such as long text that has been cut short, an icon-only button or a disabled control. Text only. If it needs actions, it becomes a popover opened by a click.
- Tooltip that follows the pointer: keeps giving information across an area. It appears when the pointer enters, follows it, and goes when the pointer leaves. Common on charts and on other self-contained elements.
- Popconfirm: the second check for an irreversible action on a single item, right where it was clicked. The path stays short and nothing else is interrupted.
- Dialog: for something the user must stop and confirm or complete before going on: an action with a large impact, one that affects other people, a bulk action, or one that needs another decision first (such as who takes over the projects). - Can the action be undone? Then don't confirm: do it at once and offer Undo (a toast, or a way back such as a trash).

- Is it a form? Short, and nothing on the page is needed for reference: dialog. Long, needs the page in view, or wants the width: drawer. The main task, or needs its own URL: a page.
- Is the information about one element, or about wherever the pointer is inside an area? One element: tooltip. An area: tooltip that follows the pointer. Either way, does it need anything to click? Then it is a popover.
- On touch screens there is no hover: anything shown on hover must also be reachable by a tap.

- Dialog: the system's modal or a native dialog opened with showModal(). Keeps focus inside and Escape cancels. It says who or what is affected and what cannot be undone. Buttons name the action ("Remove member", not "OK").
- Drawer: comes in from the edge it is attached to and leaves the page in view. Changes show up in the page behind it as they are made. Closes with Escape and a close button; focus moves into it and back out to what opened it.
- Drawers, dialogs and pages with a form: closing with unsaved changes asks first.

- Change only the kind where the current one is wrong, plus the missing behaviour from step 3.
- Don't change colours, radii, shadows, fonts, spacing or animations, and don't add new visual patterns.
- Keep copy as it is, except confirm buttons and the line that explains what cannot be undone.
- If a case needs a component the system doesn't have (an undo toast, a popover), stop and ask me before adding one.

- Before changing any code, give me a table: each use, where it is, its current kind, the kind you recommend, and why in one line.
- Mark the ones that are already right, and the ones that could fit two kinds, with what decides between them.
- Wait for my go-ahead, then make only the changes I approve and list every file you touched.

prompts.text:
Give the cards and panels in my product a liquid glass material: clear glass that takes its color from the scene behind it, reads as a thick slab at the rim, adapts to what is behind it, and keeps its text readable in light and dark mode. Work inside my existing design system. This is a change of surface, not of layout: keep my markup, spacing, radii, fonts, icons and copy.

0. Start from what exists
- Find every surface that sits over an image, a wallpaper, video or a busy background: cards, players, search bars, toolbars, menus, popovers, toasts. List them with their component and where they are.
- Find how the product switches between light and dark mode, and where its color tokens live. The glass goes into those tokens, not into each component.
- Leave surfaces over a plain background alone; glass over a flat color only looks gray.

1. The material as tokens
Build it as one set of variables per state, so a surface opts in by using them. The numbers are a starting point, for a UI at its normal size.
- Light glass, dark text (the default): tint white at 6–22% (by density, step 4); backdrop filter blur(2px) saturate(180%) brightness(1.06), so the color comes from behind and stays vivid instead of milky.
  Edge: inset 1.5px 1.5px 1px -1px white 95%, inset -1.5px -1.5px 1px -1px white 55%, inset 0 0 0 0.5px white 30%, 0 0 0 0.5px black 6%, 0 6px 24px black 8%.
  Inner light, on a layer inside the surface: a radial highlight from the top left (white 30% fading out by 55%), and soft inset glows just inside the rim, brighter at the top and left, a little shade at the bottom.
- Light mode over a dark area, light text: tint rgb(16 18 22) at 10–30%; filter blur(2px) saturate(170%), then brightness(0.85); edge: a faint inset white line on top and a 0.5px dark outline.
- Dark mode: tint rgb(20 20 24) at 16–38%; filter blur(2px) saturate(160%) brightness(0.8), which dims like a multiply with black instead of going muddy; the same edge and inner light at about a third of their strength, with a darker outline and shadow.
- Ink, one color in fixed steps, used for everything drawn on the glass:
  on light glass black 86% (titles, icons, times, progress), rgb(60 60 67) at 70% (secondary); mix-blend-mode multiply;
  on dark glass white 94%, rgb(235 235 245) at 64%; mix-blend-mode plus-lighter.
  Draw icons in the opaque color and fade the whole icon with opacity: a translucent color darkens where a shape's strokes and fills overlap.
- A highlighted row on light glass is a lighter layer of the glass: white 42% on hover, 76% when selected, with a white stroke. Never a gray wash.
- Register the numeric and color tokens with @property so a surface glides between states instead of jumping.

2. Apply it in four declarations
Each surface changes only these, and its markup stays as it is:
- background: the tint.
- backdrop-filter: the material's filter, then the rim lens (step 3) last, so the color steps fold into one pass and the bend stays crisp.
- box-shadow: the edge.
- color: the ink, with the blend mode on everything drawn inside.
Hover brightens the tint by about 14% instead of lifting a shadow.

3. The rim lens
- Build a displacement map for each surface: red is the sideways bend, green the vertical one, 128 is none. Only a rim bends; the middle stays flat.
- The rim is about 44px wide on a card (min(44px, the short side / 3.5), never under 4px). For a thick slab, a point d from the edge looks inward by 1.1 × rim × (1 - d / rim)^2.6: hard at the edge, where the scene folds back on itself, easing to nothing at the rim's inner edge.
- Draw the map for the same corner the CSS draws. If the surface uses corner-shape: superellipse(), follow that curve, not a circle, or the bend and the rim light miss each other at the corners.
- Put it in an SVG filter with feImage (the map) and feDisplacementMap (scale = 2 × the largest offset), and add url(#id) at the end of backdrop-filter.
- Split it into colors: three passes, red 15% further and blue 15% less, each kept to its channel with feColorMatrix and added back with screen blends. Check the corners of wide rims over busy backgrounds; lower the split where it turns into a haze.
- Only Chromium draws url() in backdrop-filter. Check CSS.supports('backdrop-filter', 'url(#a)') and skip Firefox, which parses it and draws nothing. Everywhere else the CSS-only glass stays.
- Wait for the map image to decode before pointing a surface at the filter, or it draws without its blur. Give every filter a unique id and its own <svg>. Build maps once per radius and rim width and reuse them; on resize, move the map, don't rebuild it.
- Skip the lens on surfaces under 32px, and on surfaces with will-change or their own compositing layer (menus, animated panels), where Chrome can draw the map instead of the bent backdrop.

4. Adapt to what is behind
- For each surface, sample the background under it at a 5 × 3 grid, drop the two darkest and two brightest points, and average. Luminance is (0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B) / 255; texture is the brightest point minus the darkest.
- Ink: in light mode, light text when the luminance is under 0.5. Keep the current ink within ±0.05 of the line so a surface never flickers at it. Dark mode is always light text. Neighbouring surfaces in one row share one decision.
- Density (0 thin, 1 dense) = 0.55 × how close the background is to the ink's own brightness + 0.7 × texture + 0.3 × chroma. It moves the tint between its thin and dense alpha.
- Saturation kept = 1 - 0.75 × chroma, at least 0.45, so a vivid background doesn't stain the glass.
- Sample again when the background, the theme or a surface's position changes, and remember the last ink so the next load opens in it.
- If the background is not an image you can read (live video, cross-origin content), pick the ink from the theme and use the dense tint.

5. Let people set the tint
- Add one setting for light mode and one for dark that scale the tint, from 0 to 1.5 (1 is the material as designed). Below 1 the brightness lift in the filter thins with it, so at 0 only the blur, the rim and the shadow are left.
- Each theme keeps its own value; switching themes glides to that theme's value.

6. Keep it accessible
- Check text contrast on the busiest and the darkest background the product allows, at the default tint; raise density, not the ink's opacity, until it passes.
- Respect prefers-reduced-transparency and forced colors: fall back to a solid surface in the same tint at full opacity.
- Keep focus rings, disabled states and error colors as they are; failures keep their red.

7. Deliver
- First list the surfaces you will change, which get the lens and the color split, and which you leave solid and why.
- Then add the tokens, the lens helper and the two settings, switch the surfaces over, and list every file you touched.
- Don't change layout, fonts, radii or copy. If a surface would need a new component to work as glass, stop and ask me first.

prompts.text:
Give the motion in my product the right easing curves, so things arrive, leave and move the way they should feel. Work inside my existing code and design system: keep what each animation does, how far it goes and what triggers it. Change how it moves over time, and its duration where that is off.

0. Start from what exists
- Find every transition and animation: CSS transitions and keyframes, animation libraries (Framer Motion, GSAP, the Web Animations API) and hand-written requestAnimationFrame loops. List each with its component, its trigger, its duration and its curve.
- Flag the ones left on the CSS default `ease`, `linear` on something that moves, and `ease-in` on something that appears.

1. The curves as tokens
Define them once, next to the other motion tokens, and use only these:
- --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0, 0, .58, 1). Anything that enters: toasts, menus, popovers, dialogs, drawers.
- --ease-out-strong: cubic-bezier(.22, 1, .36, 1). Small parts settling in right after a click: an icon, a label, a selected pill. It feels the most responsive.
- --ease-in: cubic-bezier(.42, 0, 1, 1). Anything that leaves, and only that: a toast timing out, a dialog or drawer closing, a menu collapsing, a list item swiped away. It starts slow and leaves at full speed, so on an entrance it feels late and then stops with a bump.
- --ease-in-out: cubic-bezier(.42, 0, .58, 1). Something that stays on screen and only changes place or size: the indicator under tabs or a segmented control, a carousel turning a page, items making room during a reorder, a sidebar resizing, smooth-scrolling to an anchor. Not for coming in: its slow start reads as lag.
- --ease-overshoot: cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1). Runs about 10% past its place and comes back. Small, playful confirmations: a checkbox tick, a like, a badge count popping in, a switch knob settling. Never on a dialog, a drawer or anything larger than about 64px, and not on actions people repeat all day.
- --ease-spring: linear(0, .32, .78, 1.04, 1.09, 1.06, 1.02, 1, .99, .99, 1). Things let go after a drag or a swipe, so they settle like an object: a bottom sheet snapping open or back, a card returning after a half swipe, pull-to-refresh springing back, a reordered item dropping into place. Prefer the animation library's own spring fed with the release velocity; use this token only where there is none, and fall back to --ease-out-strong where linear() is not supported.
- linear: only for things that run rather than move: spinners, progress bars, marquees.
- The CSS default `ease` is not a choice. Replace it wherever a curve was left unset.

2. Durations
- Small UI (toasts, tooltips, menus, checks): 150-250ms in, 120-200ms out. Exits are shorter than entrances.
- Medium (dialogs, popovers with content, drawers): 250-350ms.
- Large or full-screen (sheets, page transitions): 350-500ms. Longer feels slow.
- Springs and overshoots: about 1.5x the plain duration, since the settle takes time.
- Keep the durations as tokens beside the curves (--duration-sm, -md, -lg).

3. Apply them by role
- Entrances: ease-out, coming from where the thing belongs (a toast from the top edge, a menu from its trigger), over a short distance (8-24px), growing from 96% and fading in a little sooner than it moves. A light blur (about 8px) that clears as it lands is a nice touch on toasts.
- Exits: ease-in, the same path reversed, and shorter.
- Moves on screen: ease-in-out.
- Parts inside something that has just appeared (its icon, its text, a count) may follow 100-200ms later on the strong ease-out, so it lands in steps rather than all at once.
- Gestures: while the pointer or finger moves, follow it 1:1 with no easing. On release, finish on the spring, from the release velocity if the library allows.
- Hover and press: 100-150ms ease-out. Never animate layout on hover.
- Animate transform and opacity (filter sparingly), not top, left, width or height, which lay out and repaint every frame.

4. Keep it consistent and accessible
- One curve per role across the product. Don't tune each component by hand.

/* Prompt (1) */
Give the motion in my product the right easing curves, so things arrive, leave and move the way they should feel. Work inside my existing code and design system: keep what each animation does, how far it goes and what triggers it. Change how it moves over time, and its duration where that is off.

0. Start from what exists

1. The curves as tokens
Define them once, next to the other motion tokens, and use only these:

- --ease-in: cubic-bezier(.42, 0, 1, 1). Anything that leaves, and only that: a toast timing out, a dialog or drawer closing, a menu collapsing, a list item swiped away. It starts slow and leaves at full speed, so on an entrance it feels late and then stops with a bump.

✨ 012 消息气泡的材质与动效（探索版）

001–012 都在主页，关注我，每天一个让产品更有质感的小技巧。Prompt 随附，可以直接复制使用 ⬇️

为现有的聊天界面（Agent / AI 对话界面）换一种气泡材质，同时配上对应风格的思考动效和出入场动效。适合想做出自己风格、和常见界面拉开差异的产品。

6 种材质：

Cirrus：没有描边的薄磨砂玻璃，背后是蓝天白云。适合轻盈、干净的产品。

像素：气泡画在像素网格上，边缘一格一格变化，移动时带一点像素拖影。

Aqua：老 Mac 的果冻质感，表面有一层高光。

渐变：类似 Telegram 的做法，整段对话共用一张渐变，气泡所在的高度不同，颜色也不同。

拟物：和 001 的拟物按钮用同一套配方。

纯色：基础对照组，最好读，也最省性能。

items.tip:
日更栏目《999 个小技巧，让你 Vibe 的产品更有质感》

✨ 有物理质感的冲击波（含扭曲与通道分离）

iOS 27.3 加入了屏幕边缘的跑马灯光效，也让我想起用 Dia 时，每次打开主页都会出现的光环冲击效果，于是尝试把两者结合。

Prompt 附在文末，可直接复制使用 ⬇️

该效果由 6 层组成：

1. 页面快照：将当前页面转为图像，作为后续各层的计算基础（可以借助 Chrome 新增的 HTML-in-Canvas）

2. 透镜扭曲：光环整体作为一个透镜，外侧拉伸、内侧压缩，表现空间被推开。

3. 通道分离：红、蓝通道的位移分别比绿色多、少 8%，在位移处形成轻微色散，同时保持文字清晰。

4. 色环：四道色环平滑过渡，随扩散逐渐淡出，决定光环的颜色与亮度。浅色模式为染色，深色模式为加光（screen 混合）。

5. 边缘折射：光环只在内容区内扩散。到达边缘时，内容如透过玻璃斜边向边缘轻微拉伸，窗框保持不变。

6. 边线反光：光环经过时，分割线与描边短暂提亮，深色模式下更弱，使页面结构也参与其中。

共 4 组配色：Aurora 蓝紫粉桃，Halo 橙黄，Frost 薄荷绿，Spark 紫金。

prompts.text:
Add a shockwave halo to my product: when something triggers it (by default, clicking or focusing the AI input), a faint halo of light sweeps across the page from one place and fades out, bending the page a few pixels as it passes, with a slight color split, in my dark and light modes. Build it inside my code and design system; do not change what the page does or how it looks at rest. Every value below is a default to start from, not a requirement.

First look at my app (section 0). Then ask me these one at a time, offering the default each time, and wait for each answer:
1. Trigger: what starts the halo (clicking or focusing the AI input, a keyboard shortcut, sending a message, the AI starting to answer, something else), and what happens if it is triggered again while one is running (restart, or ignore).
2. Origin: where it spreads from (the AI input, a button, the bottom edge of the page, the point that was clicked, the middle of a panel), and over which area (the page's content area, one panel, the whole window). Toolbars always stay clear.
3. Layers: the color rings (section 3) are always on; ask yes or no for each of the others: the bend (section 4), the color split, the refraction at the edges, the glints on lines and borders. The bend, the split and the refraction need the page as an image (section 6), so say what each costs on my platform.
4. Colors: one of the four palettes in section 3, or my brand colors (then derive four rings, and a dark and a light version, from them), and which modes my app has.
5. The input: leave my AI input as it is (the default), or turn it into the pill that springs open with a metal edge (section 1).
Then propose how you will build it on my platform (section 6 is a starting point, not a prescription), with the cost and any fallback, and wait for my go-ahead.

0. Start from what exists
- Find the AI input, what opens or focuses it, the page container it sits in, its corner radius, any toolbars over it, and whether the app has a dark mode.
- List what the page draws with (DOM, a canvas, a native view tree, a GPU renderer) and the platform version range: this decides how the bend can be done (section 6).

1. The input (only if I chose the pill)
- At rest: a pill 300 x 44 px, radius 22, white (dark: rgb(30 30 33)), a 1px hairline, a sparkle icon, the placeholder "Ask AI about this project" in 14px and a shortcut hint on the right. It sits centered on the page's content, 48px above the page's bottom.
- On click: the pill dips to 97% for 90ms, then springs open into a card 460 x 100, radius 16, growing from its center and keeping its bottom edge where it was. Spring: progress = 1 - exp(-8t) * cos(6t) over 580ms (barely past the end, settles by the end). The card's content is laid out at its final size from the start and is revealed as it grows; it fades in from 30% of the way. Height and radius follow the same progress.
- The open card: one line of text at 15px on a 22px line, 16px from the left, the caret first and the placeholder right after it; a hairline; then a toolbar 52px tall: a round add button, a short divider, two pickers (model, mode), and on the right a voice button and the send button, all 32px.
- Shadow: wide, soft and far, not heavy: 0 0 0 1px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.09), 0 2px 4px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.04), 0 28px 64px -16px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.22). No focus ring; focus shows only as the caret.
- The metal edge: a 1px border painted with a light silver gradient, linear-gradient(120deg, rgb(238 240 243), rgb(196 202 210) 28%, rgb(241 243 245) 50%, rgb(188 195 204) 74%, rgb(233 236 239)) (dark: rgb(74 79 87) to rgb(51 55 61)), with a highlight on top: conic-gradient(from <angle>, transparent 0 280deg, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.8) 325deg, transparent 360deg). Turn the angle from -60deg to 300deg over 900ms (ease-out) as the card opens, and fade the whole edge in and out over that time (opacity sin(pi * t), at most 0.75). Mask the gradient to the border only (mask with content-box exclude).
- Closing: back to the pill in 320ms, ease-in-out.

2. The halo's shape and timing
- The halo is a circle that grows from the origin I chose. The defaults assume the origin is the AI input at the bottom of the page: the circle's center sits below the page, horizontally at the input's center and 650px below the page's bottom edge, so what shows is a wide arc rising from the bottom.
- It starts with its middle at the page's bottom (radius 650) and grows by 800px over 1000ms, so it ends just past the page's top: radius = 650 + 800 * (1 - 2^(-9t)) / (1 - 2^(-9)). That is very fast at first and slow near the far edge.
- For another origin, keep the same timing and set the start and the growth so the halo starts at the origin and ends just past the farthest edge of the area: from a point inside the area, center the circle on the point and start at a radius of 0 to 40px; from an edge, put the center beyond that edge, about two thirds of the area's width away.
- Strength over the same time: min(1, t / 0.03) * (1 - t^2.2), so it is gone by the end and fades over its slow last stretch.
- It starts on the trigger (40ms after the input starts opening, if it opens).
- It stays in the area I chose: clip it to that area, with a straight edge under any toolbar and the area's own corner radius elsewhere (12px in the demo). It must never draw over a browser or app toolbar.

3. The rings and the palettes
- Across the halo's width sit four broad rings, one color each, inside to outside. With w = 110px and x = (distance from the center - radius) / w, ring i is centered at x = i - 1.5 with weight exp(-((x - c) / 0.8)^2); the color is the weighted average of the four, so neighbors blend softly. One fade covers all four: alpha = strength * exp(-1.1 * (x / 2)^2).
- Light mode tints the page: color = mix(page, ring, alpha * 0.24) + ring * alpha * 0.24 * 0.2.
- Dark mode adds light (screen): color = 1 - (1 - page) * (1 - ring * alpha * 0.3 * 1.5).
- Palettes, rings inside to outside. Each is tuned twice: brighter and more saturated on dark, softer on light.
  Aurora (blue through violet and pink to peach)
    dark: rgb(80 140 255), rgb(160 110 255), rgb(255 110 180), rgb(255 190 140)
    light: rgb(110 150 255), rgb(180 130 255), rgb(255 130 190), rgb(255 180 120)
  Halo (orange through amber to gold, like low sun through a lens)
    dark: rgb(255 150 60), rgb(255 190 70), rgb(255 225 120), rgb(255 245 210)
    light: rgb(255 140 50), rgb(255 175 60), rgb(245 200 80), rgb(255 225 150)
  Frost (mint and aqua with a touch of lime)
    dark: rgb(80 220 175), rgb(70 195 225), rgb(180 240 150), rgb(235 255 245)
    light: rgb(40 190 150), rgb(50 170 210), rgb(140 210 90), rgb(180 235 215)
  Spark (violet into gold)
    dark: rgb(140 100 255), rgb(200 130 255), rgb(255 200 110), rgb(255 235 170)
    light: rgb(130 95 240), rgb(185 125 245), rgb(245 185 80), rgb(250 215 120)

4. The bend
- The whole halo bends the page as one lens, never ring by ring (ring by ring reads as water ripples). With z = x * 0.75: push = 7px * 2.33 * z * exp(-z^2), along the direction away from the circle's center; read the page at position - push. Outside the halo's middle the page stretches, inside it squeezes, over about the width of the rings and no wider.
- Color split: at most a trace. Read red at 1.08 times the offset and blue at 0.92 times; text must stay clean.
- The frame holds the page: fade the lens to nothing over the last 56px before the page's edge, so the edge stays straight.
- The page's lines catch the light: where the halo passes, its rules, borders and the outlines of chips, cards and nodes brighten toward the ring color (mixed 20% toward white), at the halo's strength times exp(-1.4 * (x / 2)^2) times 0.3 on light and 0.14 on dark (a faint glint, not a redrawn border), read at their bent position so the glint follows them. Text and icons never light up. To find the lines, use a second capture of the page with every rule and border drawn white at its own width on black, and nothing else (no text, icons, pictures, fills or shadows); light the page where that capture is white, so a 1px border glints as 1px. Without a capture (a retrofit in the DOM), give each bordered element and divider a CSS variable from 0 to 1 by its distance to the halo's front each frame, and mix its border color toward the ring color by it.
- The edge as a glass bevel: at the sides and the bottom (not under a toolbar), where the halo reaches the edge, read the last 60px of the page from up to 22px further in (22 * (1 - d/60)^2 * the halo's strength there), so content beside the edge stretches toward it. Where the halo meets the edge, add a thin line of light (exp(-d / 7)) in the ring color mixed 45% toward white.

5. Rhythm
- On the trigger: if the input opens, it dips to 97% for 90ms, springs open (580ms) and its edge highlight turns (900ms); the halo leaves 40ms after the opening starts and runs 1000ms. Without the input, the halo runs on the trigger.
- Switching between dark and light cross-fades the halo's colors with the page; never cut.
- Reduced motion: no bend, no split and no glints; the halo fades in and out in place at half strength over 600ms.
- Draw only while the halo runs; nothing at rest.

6. How to build it, by platform
These are suggestions from what worked in the demo and what each platform offers; check them against my stack and its versions, and choose what fits. The halo itself (the rings, and the glints on lines and edges) is only an overlay and works anywhere. The bend needs the page as an image to sample from.
- Web, as in the demo: a WebGL2 canvas over the page draws everything in one fragment pass from a snapshot of the page. Cap the pixel ratio at 2; the canvas ignores pointer events and is removed or hidden at rest.
- Web, getting the snapshot:
  - HTML-in-Canvas (WICG): a canvas with the page as its child, drawn with drawElementImage() or uploaded as a WebGL texture, live and with real browser rendering. Behind the canvas-draw-element flag in recent Chromium and reported on by default from Chrome 157; no Firefox or Safari yet. Use it where present.
  - SVG foreignObject libraries (html-to-image, modern-screenshot): the browser renders the clone, so it is faithful, but images and fonts must be inlined or same-origin, the root needs a background color, and backdrop-filter is unreliable. Take it once on click (tens to a few hundred ms), then animate.
  - html2canvas (or html2canvas-pro): it re-implements CSS on a canvas, so modern effects (backdrop-filter, some gradients, oklch) may come out wrong. A last resort.
  - Fallback without a snapshot: draw only the halo in a transparent canvas over the page (light mode: normal alpha; dark mode: mix-blend-mode: screen or plus-lighter), and skip the bend. In Chromium only, a bend is possible with backdrop-filter pointing at an SVG filter with feDisplacementMap, at a cost.
- iOS (SwiftUI, iOS 17+): put the halo in a Metal [[stitchable]] function and apply .layerEffect(shader, maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: 30, height: 30)) to the page view: it can sample the view at bent positions and add the color, live. Drive radius and strength from a TimelineView or an animatable value. Below iOS 17: an overlay with an AngularGradient and blur, without the bend.
- Android (API 33+): write the shader in AGSL as a RuntimeShader with a uniform shader named for the content, and set view.setRenderEffect(RenderEffect.createRuntimeShaderEffect(shader, "content")) on the page's root (in Compose: Modifier.graphicsLayer { renderEffect = ...asComposeRenderEffect() }). Update its uniforms every frame. Below 33: an overlay only.
- Flutter (Impeller): a FragmentProgram with ImageFilter.shader inside a BackdropFilter clipped to the page; the engine passes the content as sampler 0 and its size as the first vec2. Use FlutterFragCoord(), flip y on GLES, and check ImageFilter.isShaderFilterSupported, with an overlay-only fallback.
- Rust: render the UI into an offscreen texture, then draw one fullscreen pass with the same shader ported to WGSL that samples it.
  - wgpu by hand: render target texture with TEXTURE_BINDING usage, a fullscreen triangle, uniforms in one buffer.
  - Bevy: a custom post-processing node; call post_process_write() on the ViewTarget to get the source and destination textures, as in Bevy's custom post-processing example.
  - egui or iced on wgpu: render the frame into a texture through the renderer's wgpu callback and composite with the shader; their widgets cannot sample what is under them by themselves.
- Electron and Tauri: the web route; Electron can also take a snapshot with webContents.capturePage().

7. Check
- Dark and light, in the colors I chose: the text under the halo stays readable and unsplit; the halo never shows on a toolbar; the area's corners stay clean; the bend is no wider than the rings.
- The trigger and the origin are the ones I chose, and the page works exactly as before.
- It runs only while the halo is visible and costs nothing at rest.
